methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes source structure (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/OT.json), corrected against raw OCR of the chapter's own TOC (pdf 1145) and ~20 body pages. Unlike OR's genuine two-column TOC corruption, OT's toc_inventory.json extraction is single-column and largely clean; the defects found here are three distinct, spot-verified anomalies: (1) a body heading entirely absent from toc_inventory.json and independently flagged as OT's one UNRESOLVED entry in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json -- a real 'Hearing' section (TN OT9-OT12, pdf 1153-1156) covering hearing physiology, DDx, bedside/audiometric testing, and aural rehabilitation, confirmed via raw OCR and represented as SU-OT-04/05 under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id; (2) a mislabeled/mis-anchored section node, OT.S04 (captured title 'Tinnitus', start pdf 1160/OT16), whose body content at that page is actually 'Diseases of the External Ear' (matching the node's own merged_duplicate_headings field) -- the real, separate one-page 'Tinnitus' section (Definition/History/Investigations/Treatment) is an undetected body heading on pdf 1159 (OT15), confirmed via raw OCR and represented as SU-OT-06 under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id; and (3) a body-heading-assigned-to-wrong-parent defect analogous to OR's Spine-under-References finding -- OT.S07.T01/T02 ('Allergic Rhinitis', 'Vasomotor Rhinitis') are captured as children of OT.S07 (titled 'Facial Nerve'), but raw OCR of pdf 1166-1168 (OT22-OT24) confirms OT.S07's real, full title is 'Facial Nerve (CN VII) Paralysis' (ending on OT23 with Bell's Palsy/Ramsay Hunt content and no rhinitis content at all), and that Allergic/Vasomotor Rhinitis are real children of a separate 'Rhinitis' section header (Table 11/12: rhinitis classification and nasal-discharge differential) that is itself absent from toc_inventory.json -- represented as SU-OT-27 (corrected Facial Nerve unit) and SU-OT-28/29/30 (recovered Rhinitis section, with T01/T02 re-parented). All three corrections are resolved via raw OCR body-page confirmation (never model memory/medical-knowledge reconstruction) and cited in each affected unit's structural_rationale; no page-image rendering was required as raw-text OCR was internally consistent and sufficient at every point checked. Excluded as non-clinical organizational/reference material: the chapter root (OT) and OT.S16 (Common Medications, a drug-reference table, consistent with the OR.S15/OP.S20/OB.S18/NS.S20 reference-section precedent); the Acronyms portion of OT.S01 is likewise excluded, consistent with the OP.S01/OB.S01/NS.S01/OR.S01 chapter-opening acronym-glossary precedent, while its co-located 'Basic Anatomy Review' content is retained as SU-OT-01.

study_units.title: Basic Anatomy Review (Ear, Nose, Throat, Head and Neck)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S01's captured title 'Acromyms' (OCR-garbled 'Acronyms') matches the chapter-opening acronym-glossary pattern seen in OP.S01/OB.S01/NS.S01/OR.S01; raw OCR of pdf 1146-1149 (OT2-OT5) body-confirms the acronym table is immediately followed by the real 'Basic Anatomy Review' content (external/middle/inner ear anatomy, nasal anatomy, laryngeal anatomy, facial nerve branches, neck anatomy and anatomical triangles) matching the T01-T05 topic children (Ear, Nose, Throat, Head and Neck, Anatomical Triangles of the Neck). The non-clinical acronym glossary itself is excluded from study units per the established precedent.

source_hierarchy_path: Dizziness / Evaluation of the Dizzy Patient

study_units.title: Approach to Otalgia (Primary vs. Referred Ear Pain)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S02.T02 (Otalgia, DDx Figure 12: external/middle/inner ear causes vs. referred pain) is a standalone approach unit; raw OCR of pdf 1151 (OT7) confirms the associated '10 Ts of Referred Pain' sidebar (Teeth, TMD, Tubal area, Tonsils, Throat, Tongue, Trachea, Thyroid, Temporal arteritis, Trauma) as real chapter content.

study_units.title: Approach to Hearing Loss (Physiology, DDx, Bedside Tuning Fork Tests)
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json captures OT.S02.T03 (Hearing Loss DDx, Figure 13) but has no node at all for the real 'Hearing' section heading printed in the chapter TOC (raw OCR of pdf 1145: 'Hearing... OT9', between 'Neck Mass' and 'Vertigo... OT12'); this is also research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json's one UNRESOLVED entry for OT ('Hearing', page-anchor could not be confirmed). Resolved via raw OCR of pdf 1153-1154 (OT9-OT10): the section opens with 'Normal Hearing Physiology', 'Types of Hearing Loss' (conductive/sensorineural/mixed), and 'Auditory Acuity' (whispered-voice test, Rinne and Weber tuning fork tests with Table 4 interpretation), ending before 'Pure Tone Audiometry'. This physiology/DDx/bedside-test portion is grouped with the DDx figure as the generalist-relevant half of the recovered section; the audiometric-technology portion is split into SU-OT-05 below.

study_units.title: Audiometric Testing and Aural Rehabilitation (Pure Tone, Speech, Impedance, ABR, OAE, Hearing Aids)
source_hierarchy_path: Pure Tone Audiometry / Speech Audiometry / Impedance Audiometry / Auditory Brainstem Response / Otoacoustic Emissions / Aural Rehabilitation
study_units.structural_rationale: Second half of the same body-recovered 'Hearing' section (see SU-OT-04 for the missing-node rationale): raw OCR of pdf 1154-1156 (OT10-OT12) confirms 'Pure Tone Audiometry', 'Speech Audiometry', 'Impedance Audiometry' (tympanogram types A/B/C, static compliance, acoustic stapedial reflexes), 'Auditory Brainstem Response', 'Otoacoustic Emissions', and 'Aural Rehabilitation' (hearing aid types, cochlear implants) as real consecutive headings ending immediately before 'Evaluation of the Dizzy Patient' begins the Vertigo section.

study_units.title: Tinnitus (DDx, Definition, History, Investigations, Management)
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's OT.S04 node (title 'Tinnitus', start pdf 1160/OT16) is a mislabeled/mis-anchored heading: raw OCR of pdf 1160 (OT16) body-confirms the section actually beginning there is 'Diseases of the External Ear' (Cerumen Impaction, Exostoses, Otitis Externa, Malignant Otitis Externa -- see SU-OT-13/14/15), matching the node's own merged_duplicate_headings field ('Diseases of the ExtermalEar'). The real, separate 'Tinnitus' body section (Definition, History, Investigations, Treatment -- e.g. 'unilateral tinnitus or SNHL is acoustic neuroma until proven otherwise') is confirmed via raw OCR of pdf 1159 (OT15), immediately after 'Acoustic Neuroma' ends the Vertigo section and before 'Diseases of the External Ear' begins -- a body heading entirely absent from toc_inventory.json. Grouped here with the Tinnitus DDx figure (OT.S02.T04, Figure 14: subjective vs. objective/pulsatile tinnitus).

study_units.title: Approach to a Neck Mass (DDx by Age, Evaluation)

study_units.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S03.T02 title 'Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo' is clean/unmerged; page range inherited from the parent Vertigo section (OT.S03, pdf 1156-1159) as the specific BPPV heading page was not individually OCR-spot-checked.

study_units.title: Meniere's Disease (Endolymphatic Hydrops)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S03.T03's captured title is OCR-garbled ('Meéniere's Disease') but unambiguous; raw OCR of pdf 1158 (OT14) body-confirms episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency SNHL, tinnitus, and aural fullness as the classic tetrad, with Tumarkin drop attacks in later disease.

study_units.title: Vestibular Neuronitis (Labyrinthitis)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S03.T04 title is clean/unmerged; raw OCR of pdf 1158 (OT14) body-confirms acute-onset disabling vertigo with nausea/vomiting and imbalance, without hearing loss (vestibular neuronitis) vs. with hearing loss (labyrinthitis), typically post-viral.

study_units.title: Acoustic Neuroma (Vestibular Schwannoma)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S03.T05 title is clean/unmerged; raw OCR of pdf 1159 (OT15) body-confirms unilateral SNHL or tinnitus as the usual presentation, with the explicit teaching point 'unilateral tinnitus or SNHL is acoustic neuroma until proven otherwise' in the elderly, and gadolinium-enhanced MRI as the diagnostic gold standard.

study_units.title: Cerumen Impaction and Exostoses
study_units.structural_rationale: Children of OT.S04, whose section title is corrected to 'Diseases of the External Ear' (see SU-OT-06 for the full structural-correction rationale). Raw OCR of pdf 1160 (OT16) confirms Cerumen Impaction (most common cause of CHL age 15-50) and Exostoses (bony EAC protuberances, usually incidental) as consecutive real headings.

study_units.title: Otitis Externa
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S04.T03 title is clean/unmerged; raw OCR of pdf 1160 (OT16) confirms bacterial (90%, most commonly Pseudomonas aeruginosa) etiology, tragal/pinna traction tenderness as the classic exam finding, and topical antipseudomonal therapy (avoiding ototoxic topical agents if the TM is perforated) as first-line treatment.

study_units.title: Malignant (Necrotizing) Otitis Externa (Skull Base Osteomyelitis)
study_units.structural_rationale: OT.S04.T04 title is clean/unmerged; raw OCR of pdf 1160-1161 (OT16-OT17) confirms this as a medical emergency occurring in elderly diabetic/immunocompromised patients, almost always caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with cranial nerve palsy as a feared complication.

study_units.title: Facial Nerve (CN VII) Paralysis (Bell's Palsy vs. Ramsay Hunt Syndrome)
study_units.structural_rationale: STRUCTURAL CORRECTION: toc_inventory.json's OT.S07 node is captured with title 'Facial Nerve' and two T-children, 'Allergic Rhinitis (i.e. Hay Fever)' and 'Vasomotor Rhinitis', that are clinically unrelated to facial nerve disease. Raw OCR of pdf 1166-1167 (OT22-OT23) body-confirms: (1) the section's real, full title is 'Facial Nerve (CN VII) Paralysis' (matching the TOC line 'Facial Nerve (CN VIl) Paralysis...OT22'), covering Central Facial Paralysis (cross-ref 'see Neurology, N3'), Peripheral Facial Paralysis/Bell's Palsy (KITTENS etiology mnemonic), and Table 10 (Bell's Palsy vs. Ramsay Hunt Syndrome); and (2) this section ends on OT23 with no Allergic/Vasomotor Rhinitis content anywhere in it. 'Allergic Rhinitis' and 'Vasomotor Rhinitis' are real body headings that instead begin immediately after, under a missing 'Rhinitis' section header not captured in toc_inventory.json (Table 11: Classification of Rhinitis; Table 12: Nasal Discharge) -- see SU-OT-28/29/30 for that recovered section. This is a body-heading-assigned-to-wrong-parent defect (the extraction pipeline evidently attributed the next TOC row's page anchor and following body content to the prior section once its own children ran out), analogous to the OR.S16 Spine-re-parented-under-References defect. OT.S07.T01/T02 are re-parented here to their real parent (the recovered Rhinitis section).
